reviewChoiceGroups.title: Architecture disposition
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose how to handle the architecture findings for Travel Split's local data plan.

options.label: Use reduced snapshot repository
options.description: Proceed with current tabs, TripDataProvider, pure reducer/domain modules, and a snapshot-in-IndexedDB TripRepository.
options.rationale: This satisfies local DB and SQLite-later goals while avoiding premature normalized IndexedDB complexity.

options.label: Keep normalized IndexedDB
options.description: Implement trips, people, expenses, metadata stores and tripId queries in the first pass.
options.rationale: Use this only if multiple-trip or SQLite-style schema rehearsal is more important than a smaller first green path.

options.label: Return to original localStorage contract
options.description: Ignore the latest IndexedDB preference and implement the original localStorage adapter.
options.rationale: This is smallest relative to the original docs, but conflicts with the user's new local database decision.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Code quality stance
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the implementation discipline for domain, provider, and screen wiring.

options.label: Clean domain boundaries
options.description: Add domain types, parsers, reducer, selectors, logger, repository, and keep screens presentation-oriented.
options.rationale: The review found mock DTOs and inline form state cannot safely support real split math.

options.label: Provider-heavy fast path
options.description: Put most parsing, selectors, persistence, and logging directly in TripDataProvider for speed, refactor later.
options.rationale: Fastest implementation, but likely creates a God module and weaker unit-test boundaries.

options.label: Inline screen logic
options.description: Wire commands and validation directly inside PeopleScreen, ExpensesScreen, and SettleScreen.
options.rationale: Lowest indirection, but contradicts the reviewed requirement to keep calculation rules outside React components.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Validation requirement
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the validation gate required before accepting implementation.

options.label: Full reduced verify gate
options.description: Require Vitest coverage at 80%, repository tests with fake IndexedDB, build, and one Playwright screenshot smoke test.
options.rationale: This directly covers money math, reducer behavior, persistence, and runtime wiring without a broad e2e suite.

options.label: Unit + build only
options.description: Run Vitest coverage and production build, but skip browser screenshot automation.
options.rationale: Simpler bootstrap, but fails the selected runtime/browser validation requirement.

options.label: Manual browser proof
options.description: Run unit/build automatically and validate UI manually with a screenshot.
options.rationale: Lower dependency load, but not repeatable and weaker at catching mock-data wiring regressions.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Performance and risk response
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose how implementation should handle local DB failure, logs, and privacy risk.

options.label: Visible errors + redacted logs
options.description: Add provider load/save error states, command-scoped saves, safe structured console logs, and synthetic screenshot data.
options.rationale: This closes the two critical gaps: silent save failure and clipboard failure, while keeping logs console-only.

options.label: Console-only failures
options.description: Log IndexedDB and clipboard errors to console but keep UI fallback minimal.
options.rationale: Easier to implement, but creates silent user-facing data loss risk.

options.label: Persistent audit log
options.description: Store local event logs alongside trip data for debugging.
options.rationale: Useful later, but explicitly outside the selected console-only logging scope and adds privacy/storage complexity.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Final disposition
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the final implementation decision for this exit review.

options.label: Approve reduced scope
options.description: Implement the snapshot IndexedDB repository plan with the must-do guardrails before coding.
options.rationale: The plan is implementation-ready after reducing storage complexity and reconciling stale docs.

options.label: Request plan addendum first
options.description: Do not implement until the contract file is updated to remove localStorage/workspace contradictions.
options.rationale: Useful if stale documentation is likely to mislead the implementation pass.

options.label: Reject for redesign
options.description: Stop and redesign around normalized IndexedDB or SQLite before any UI wiring.
options.rationale: Use only if the local DB schema is considered the primary product risk.
